articleTitle: Design and Development of Innovation-based Learning for Advanced Digital System Course
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of innovation-based learning for advanced digital system course that is a key role to start innovating in the future digital realworld lifestyle. The objective of this research is to prepare the computer engineering students through the use of local market devices applied for real-world mini-projects. Development of this course aims to improve both hard- and soft-skills as technical abilities, problem solving, critical thinking, collaboration, and leadership. The learning outcome of this course is to prepare the junior students with an in-depth knowledge of digital integrated circuit hardware design for doing the final project. The evaluation shows that students can improve and understand that the basic knowledge of this course is the first step of successful innovation in the future.

articleTitle: Engineering Teacher Training using MIAP Based Coaching and Mentoring Techniques in Promoting Teacher Competencies
abstract: The purposes of this research were 1) to manage engineering teacher training using the MIAP learning process and coaching and mentoring techniques, 2) to assess the competencies of electrical engineering teachers by using the developed teaching and learning management, 3) to evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and learning management, and 4) to evaluate learners' satisfaction using the developed teaching and learning management. The purposive sample group of this research was 27 bachelor teacher students, Department of Teacher Training in Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Technical Education at King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. The research results shown that 1) results of the evaluation in teacher students' skill was higher than 75%, 2) the performance of the developed teaching model shown that learning process (E1) and learning achievement (E2) were higher than 75%, and 3) the learners' satisfaction with the developed learning and teaching process was at a high level (the mean equaled to 4.38).

articleTitle: Students' Perception of Online Classes and Exams Held During COVID-19 Pandemic: The Engineering Faculty's Experience at Assumption University
abstract: This paper is an expansion of a previous study into the challenges and perceptions associated with online delivery of engineering courses at Assumption University of Thailand (AU) during the global Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. AU maintained continuity of its learning activities by switching program delivery across all faculties to a fully online mode from the middle of March, 2020. To measure the effectiveness of the online learning mode, AU's engineering faculty students were sent three questionnaire-based online surveys to offer their feedback on online classes and exams conducted during the emergency closure. While a majority of the online engineering courses (approximately 64%) received favorable evaluation by students, it was deemed that certain factors (e.g. infrastructure, instructor empathy, exam format, unsuitability for hands-on classes) could negatively impact students' perception of online learning. Emotional well-being of the students during the crisis was not assessed as a factor potentially influencing their survey responses, but could be included in future.

articleTitle: Hybrid learning during the COVID-19 pandemic of engineering students at KMITL, Thailand
abstract: This article presents the hybrid learning model during the COVID-19 for students of Agro-Industrial Systems Engineering who enrolled in the course embedded system, course code 01386304, Faculty of Engineering, King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang for 29 students by selecting a specific sample group. The researcher presented a hybrid learning model during the COVID-19, where students were orientated for the same understanding and followed by teaching as active learning formed project-based learning. Finally, we assessed five aspects of hybrid learning satisfaction during the COVID-19. The evaluation results revealed that the students' satisfaction was at a good level and their arithmetic mean was 4.206 and the standard deviation is equal to 0.74 (X = 4.206, S.D. = 0.74)

articleTitle: Fab Lab Initiative in Higher Education: Digital Solutions Diverted to Traditional Farming in Cambodia Context
abstract: In Cambodia, after graduated from STEM university, the students apply for a STEM job and then work for industries or technological companies. Since Cambodia currently is not a manufacturing country, most of the fresh graduates work as system designers in building, installation or sale engineers using imported end global end-use products and solutions that is not fully compatible with Cambodia context. Moreover, a target of those private companies is in the urban cities rather than the rural area. This paper is to initiate an open fabrication laboratory or Fab Lab for a multipurpose small-scale fabrication in higher education, and to encourage the students to engage community-based, scenario-based and project-based learning, and also maker movement to create new digital products or ICT systems responding to their community issues through this small factory. Traditional farming is the first paradigm for this purpose to seek problem-solving and provide a digital solution to farmers. This may be oriented student's perspective in the future career after university's life.

articleTitle: User Experience and Usability of Conducting Examination via Google Classroom: A Case Study of NIDA Business School MBA Students
abstract: During the COVID-19 Pandemic, new normal practices have been applied to all usual activities including organizing examinations. During the first and second semesters of 2020 academic year at NIDA Business School, online examination via Google Classroom was used in 10 sessions of the Financial and Managerial Accounting course. To measure the NIDA MBA students' experience and usability of examination via Google Classroom, the Short User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ-S) and System Usability Scale (SUS) was employed to construct the online survey questionnaire. The result shows that 208 NIDA MBA students have had a good experience of examination via Google Classroom.

articleTitle: Active Learning Management based on MIAP Learning Model to Enhance Electronic Technician Competence
abstract: This research aims to 1) to compare the pretest and posttest achievement of learners who learn with Active learning management based on MIAP Learning model. 2) to evaluate learners' satisfaction towards learning using the developed learning and teaching process. The Sample groups of the research were 35 the second-year learners in vocational certificate curriculum, department of electronic technical at Nakhon nayok Technical College. Research instruments include 1) lesson plan using active learning management based on MIAP learning model in IC circuit and application subject, 2) instructional media, 3) achievement tests and 4) a questionnaire on learners' opinions of learning and teaching process. The research results shown that 1) the posttest of learning achievement was significantly higher than pretest at the. 05 level, 2) the learners' satisfaction with the developed learning and teaching process was at a high level (the mean equaled to 4.22).

articleTitle: Development of block-based coding teaching tool with agriculture application (Smart farm)
abstract: This study aims to build and install an irrigation system for a rectangular vegetable plot at Wat Rang Sanae Nakhon Chan school, Ratchaburi, Thailand. The motion of the water spray nozzle is similar to CNC machines with linear movements in two horizontal directions and it must be easily controlled by block-based coding suitable for Grade 5–6 students. The advantages of block-based controlled irrigation system are to promote teaching and learning in computational science at the elementary level for students to experience tangible programming results which should enhance learning outcome retention. The Smart Farm device performance assessment consists of nozzle head position accuracy, water content accuracy and usability of web interface with the m Block software, all of which have shown satisfactory results during the tests. A survey result taken by teachers and students during an on-site test shows high level of satisfaction in ease of use and practicality for education.

articleTitle: Development of Outcome-based Learning and Analytical Thinking on Basic Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an analytical thinking and an outcome-based learning (OBL) in the course of electronics for computer engineering students. A student-centered education is used with the efforts for understanding the analytical thinking on basic electronics in order to develop the soft-skills of students within knowledge management. Based on the digital real-world, the electronic devices are applied widely on many applications while basic electronics is ignored. The objective of this paper is to introduce mainly the basic electronics on computer engineering course. Based on OBL approach, the teaching effectiveness and student outcomes are evaluated by the results of assessment. Results show that students can achieve the basic knowledge on electronics, even it is hard to improve the analytical thinking within a course of basic electronics. Moreover, this development is a fundamental knowledge for the computer engineering students to create an innovation in the electrical engineering field for the future.

articleTitle: The Development of a Self-Study System for Language Learning - Overview of the Project and Related Work-
abstract: In Japan, the importance of teaching English and programming languages has been pointed out. However, no studies have analyzed both languages at the same time. In addition, the level of understanding of learners should differ from learner to learner, but the current e-learning system only presents pre-prepared tasks to all learners. We aim to develop a self-study system fortified with an artificial teacher that advises students by understanding their learning conditions. Such a system can act as a unified framework for evaluating language learning. In this study, we give an overview of previous related work and describe our research and development.

articleTitle: Development of Remote Laboratory for Feedback Control System Class
abstract: This research presents a low cost web-based remote laboratory system for a feedback control system class. The system is created by an inexpensive single-board computer (Raspberry Pi 3B+) as laboratory server, an edge of extinct Lego Mindstorms set as a controlled plant, and an IP camera system. The laboratory server based on Ubuntu, which is a free and open-source software and the web application is written with JavaScript based on a MEAN stack platform. The proposed laboratory is used for verifying a design project of the angle control system using Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control.

articleTitle: Improvement on Basic Digital System Design using Problem-based and Outcome-based Learning
abstract: This paper presents how to develop the course of digital system design with an outcome-based learning (OBL) and problem-based learning (PBL). According to improvement the hard and soft skills, the student-centered education is applied within knowledge management. Digital system design course is the compulsory and basic subject for electrical engineering to allow students understanding and controlling about the realworld digital. The objective of this paper is to introduce how to design the course of digital system design based on OBL and PBL methods including with the simulation test and assembling the prototype circuits on the digital logic trainer board. Experiment design of this course is to follow the learning outcomes with PBL approach. The teaching effectiveness and student outcomes are evaluated by the results of assessment. Experiment results and the assessment show that students can achieve significantly the basic knowledge on digital system design.

articleTitle: Determination of Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC) of Surfactants by Contact Angle Measurement Method
abstract: By using a simple USB digital microscope equipped with a vertically adjustable stand and a physic concept of surface tension, a contact angle goniometer instrument was constructed with an aim of determining the critical micelle concentration (CMC) of the surfactants in everyday usage such as dishwashing solution and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). The surfactants trap dirt and strains by micelles formation and removing dirt at concentration beyond the value at the CMC point. The CMC value can be extracted from the intersecting point between the two different linear fits of the contact angle as a function of the surfactant concentration, using image processing software and simple mathematic calculation. These CMC values of those cleaning agents are extremely helpful to reduce the use of excess chemicals and waste into an environment. In combination with the STEM concept, this instrument provides a simple design, easy to construct with high accuracy results. This interdisciplinary concept can be demonstrated as an excellent STEM tool for school or university students to explore the scientific phenomena at the surface which is no need for expensive equipment.

articleTitle: Management of Learning Activities to Promote SystematicThinking Skills for Student Teachers Training in Technology Education
abstract: The research paper presents to design and manage learning activities to promote systematic thinking skills for student teachers in technology education. The research and development process are divided into three steps: 1) designing learning activities according to the 3A-3Q teaching process to enhance systemic thinking skills, 2) experimenting with learning activities based on the developed teaching process, and 3) analyzing and concluding the research. The sample group in the research was 40 student teacher students, Bachelor of Science in Technical Education, Program in Electrical Engineering, King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok. The results of the research found that; 1) the learning activities according to the 3A-3Q teaching technique developed as assessed by 5 experts were appropriate at a high level, 2) the learners had a learning achievement in system thinking skills with an average of 78%, and 3) the satisfaction level of the learners towards the developed teaching process was at a high level. Therefore, it can be concluded that systematic thinking is an essential skill for apprenticing in technology education and is able to apply in teaching practice to produce technicians and industrial technologists with 21st century learning skills.

articleTitle: The Development of Online Learning and Teaching Management in English Literature Using Google Classroom for the Undergraduate Students
abstract: The purposes of this study aimed to; 1) to develop the online learning and teaching in English literature using Google Classroom; 2) to compare the students' English literature ability before and after using the online learning and teaching management; and 3) to study the students' opinions towards online learning and teaching management using Google Classroom. The sample group included 25 third-year students majoring in English Teaching Programme at the faculty of education, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University, selected by using the purposive sampling technique. The research instruments were 1) lesson plans, 2) pre-test and post-test, 3) classroom observation form, and 4) a Likert scale questionnaire on students' attitudes towards online learning and teaching management using Google Classroom. The statistics were mean, percentage, standard deviation, and t-test with one sample test. The research findings were 1) The students' post-test score were higher than the pre-test. The results were statistically significant difference at 0.05 level; and 2) The students' opinions towards the online learning and teaching management using Google Classroom were at the highest level (X = 4.63, S.D. = 0.55), including 1) The learning management (X = 4.80, S.D = 0.41), 2) The objectives (X =4.75, S.D = 0.44), and 3) The content (X = 4.67, S.D = 0.35) respectively. Overall, the majority provided positive responses to questionnaire items.

articleTitle: An Integrated Learning of Communication and Presentation for Industrial Work through Seminar for Special Project Preparation Using Phenomenon-Based Learning Approach
abstract: This article aims at proposing a model of learning management applying the phenomenon-based learning approach with the objective of developing knowledge and skills of the students. The approach was applied to the integration of Seminar for Special Project Preparation and Communication and Presentation for Industrial Work courses to enhance communication and presentation skills that are necessary for the 21st century industrial technology and Industry 4.0 labor market. The study was conducted to explore phenomenon in real situation of special project preparation together with learning activities on the basis of cooperative problem-solving. The research found that the model of learning management helped the students construct their own knowledge, enhance communication, presentation, information technology, report writing, and cooperative problem-solving skills. Moreover, the students can develop systematic, critical, analytical, and creative thinking skills.

articleTitle: Management of Laboratory-Based Learning Activity on Electronic Flight Instrument System
abstract: The purpose of research was to manage laboratory-based learning activity on Electronics Flight Instrument System (EFIS) based on the ARINC 429 protocol. The research tools consist of the teacher’ manual, experiment package of aircraft including the ARINC 429 standard, EFIS simulator and perturbator interface, and achievement test. The learning activities is based on practicing laboratory using aircraft equivalents and simulator. An aircraft maintenance technician should understand ARINC 429 standard which defines the physical and electrical interfaces of a two-wire data bus and a data protocol to support an avionics system on aircraft. The learning and teaching of the ARINC 429 protocol based EFIS simulator system encourage aircraft technician to able in repairing and maintaining the EFIS system on aircraft as efficiently. The research results shown that the experts' opinions on the laboratory-based learning process were found reasonably at a high level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\bar{X} =4.34)$</tex>. The students' satisfaction in learning and teaching activities of avionics engineering course was at high level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\bar{X} 4.25)$</tex>.

articleTitle: Combination of problem-based learning and case-based learning in SQL Programming for data analysis
abstract: The 21st century, the need to develop students to learn continuously. This paper presents the combination methods between case-based learning and problem-based learning in the SQL programming for data analysis. Firstly, the case-based learning will apply for the beginning such as the basic command. Secondly, problem based learning will apply to practice analyzing from real world problem. At the end of the class, the presentation of all students had to be show to learn each other. The goal of this research is to build students abilities to make their own assumptions from problems taken from the real world and use SQL programs to properly analyze their hypotheses.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Practical Pedagogy For the Youths in Special Economic Development Zone Mukdahan of Thailand
abstract: In order to search the modern pedagogy methods is challenging for how to knowledge development in modern digital disruption technology. The studying via workshop base learning is a key role to support the modern learning and integral with modern technology. This article proposed the Artificial Intelligent (AI) practical pedagogy. The sample group were the youths to study in the special economic zone of Mukdahan province 200 students. Firstly, considered course description and activities learning by motivation via lecture with workshop module, basic programming by the Python program and study programming rule base decision algorithm for control temperature and apply with Internet of Things (IOT). Secondly, evaluation achievement with tests form. The third, performing and analysis with Z-test. The results found that the practical pedagogy module and teaching platform has enhancement significantly at. 01, can be improved the pedagogy of AI basic practical and positively an innovation in the future.

articleTitle: Building LoRaWAN IoT Kits for STEM Education in Interdisciplinary Training Programs
abstract: This paper focuses on building an IoT kits based on LoRaWAnwireless communication technology for STEM in higher education. In this manner, LoraWAN-based IoT kits are designed and proposed for teaching and learning STEM interdisciplinary training programs according to current curriculums at Hue University of Sciences. This paper also shows the trend of using contemporary technologies used in STEM higher education for the current digital transformation applications in smart areas.

articleTitle: Fall warning machine with image processing via the Internet of things
abstract: The fall detection system in the elderly is an imperative system in trend of increasing the number of the elderly population, but many of the systems that are presented are not available in all areas. Wearing a device with the person being tracked makes routine activities less difficult. This research presents another way to solve this problem by using the principles of image processing. All processing systems will run only on the processing device. And send the report only the result of falling out in order to certify that the image data Will not be published in this regard, the test was conducted to study the effects. The perspective of installing a camera or even the effect of wearing clothing is similar to the color of the background during a fall.

articleTitle: Learning Process during the COVID-19 Crisis, Selected Topics in Telecommunication Engineering subject, Department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, RUS, Thailand
abstract: This article presents a learning process during the COVID-19 crisis, used in selected topics of telecommunication engineering subject, department of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Architecture Rajamangala University of Technology Suvarnabhumi. The sample consisted of 19 students, enrolled in the selected topics of telecommunication engineering course by selecting a specific sample group. The researcher presented a learning process during the COVID-19 crisis with the orientation of students for the same understanding and then teaching according to the given process. Finally, there are three aspects of satisfaction with learning processs during the COVID-19crisis assessed. The results showed that in all of the three aspects, having a very good level of students' satisfaction with an arithmetic mean of 4.614 and a standard deviation of 0.46 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{X}=4.614$</tex>, S.D. = 0.46)

articleTitle: Development of the quadruped robot modeling and movement simulation for Education
abstract: This research was aimed to developed the quadruped robot modelling and movement simulation and to test and summarize the 3D simulated quadruped robot movement. The development of the simulate quadruped robot had 5 steps, 1) structure design, 2) analyze the robot kinematics, 3) simulate the robot movement 4) LabVIEW test run to simulate the 3D movement. 5) used the quadruped robot as teaching media in industrial robotics courses and program development. From the testing result, the 3D simulated quadruped robot able to move in 6 movement, walk backward and 10 meter/minute walk forward. After used the quadruped robot in teaching, found the overall satisfaction with the teaching materials of the quadruped robot was at a good level. (X = 3.51, S.D. = 0.73). The robot suitable for use as a teaching material in courses related to robotics and encourage students to learn as well.

articleTitle: A Constructionism-Based Learning Framework to Promote EMT Conduit Bending Practice Skills
abstract: The objective of this article is to organize learning and practicing model on the basis of the constructionism-based learning framework with a view to minimize the weakness of the practice of the EMT conduit bending. This framework stimulates systematic thinking skills among the students who implements it into the realization of their projects. The tools include a teacher manual, laboratory sheets, a practice set, test sheets, and a VDO clip. The model was experimented with the students of the Faculty of Industrial Technology, Chitralada Technology Institute. The results reveal that the model triggered the participation of the students in learning activities, promoted adequate knowledge and skills. Furthermore, after comparing existing and newly acquired knowledges, the students value the learning, understand the lessons better, and are able to implement the knowledge into practice leading to the effectiveness of the project realization, the reduction of damage during the practicing.

articleTitle: Encouraging Student-Centred STEM Learning in HE: A theory-based project in Asia
abstract: Student-Centered Learning (SCL) is a way to motivate students to learn, which in this project is applied to STEM education at university level. This paper presents experiences with running a project based on a theory-driven approach to inspire change towards SCL in three Asian countries. The ultimate aim with the project is that the students develop relevant professional competencies in their STEM subjects.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Digital Medical Student Characteristics
abstract: The objective of this paper is to study, analyze and synthesize the characteristics of medical students together with digital competencies. It can be concluded that there are 4 characteristics of digital medical students: 1) Digital technology ethics 2) The use of digital technology 3) Creativity, innovation, and digital communication 4) Digital leadership. A compelling visual model is presented that defines the characteristics of medical students needed to become global citizens in the digital era.

articleTitle: Through the eyes of a research team: Using theory to enhance STEM Education
abstract: Computing Education Research (CER) is an example of Discipline-Based Education Research (DBER) that has developed substantively over the last few decades. This is especially true for the Uppsala Computing Education Research Group (UpCERG). In this paper, we use UpCERG as a lens to see how a conscious use of theory can enhance the quality of STEM education. This is accomplished through presenting our use of the concept “theory” in the paper and by using the theses produced by the group as a way to illustrate the increased importance of theoretical development.

articleTitle: Proposed Model of STEM Associated with Social Issues: Case Study on Tapioca Drip Irrigation System
abstract: The model of STEM associated with social issues is presented. Many projects are implemented with science, technology, mathematics, and engineering (STEM) but exclude the impact of long-term sustainability in both social and economic topics. The proposed model of STEM, which includes social matters, should be applied to be S+STEM. A case study of PV water pumps in the tapioca drip irrigation system has been provided to ensure the success of S+STEM. Although the design of irrigation systems requires STEM principles, it should be considered on issues related to society and communities, particularly about the cost and pollution that occur, which is a matter that the community values.

articleTitle: Competencies e-portfolio construction and defense influence on STEM career choice
abstract: This paper analyzes the competency portfolio from high-school students in Tecnologico de Monterrey, in State of Mexico and compare their declared mastery level of specific competencies with their career choice. The research design is quantitative, measuring high school competencies e-portfolio influence on STEM career choice. It analyses the e-portfolios from 64 students in their last high school year. The competency portfolio is the compilation of evidence that demonstrate the mastery of competencies, we analyzed the most common competencies in them and relate them to the career choice. The results indicates that the perceived self-efficacy is higher in students who choose engineering areas and that projects, philanthropy actions and international experiences favors the self-efficacy perception.

articleTitle: Application of CDIO Initiative on High-Skill Workforce Development to Reduce Losses in Production Process
abstract: The technician who works in industry is an important manpower who mainly supports operator in term of machine service. The good service affects to reduction of breakdown time and production loss. Application of the CDIO initiative on high-skill workforce development, to reduce losses in the production process, is proposed in this paper. Based on CDIO process, high-skill workforces or technicians were trained to think in deep both theory and practice in order to develop problem solving and systematic thinking skill. Implementation and results are presented in this paper. And it shows that the CDIO initiative is a powerful tool not only for engineering education but high-skill workforce development also. Production loss reduction is represented and this is one of key performance index for indicating an effectiveness of training.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study of Virtual Telehealth Game
abstract: The objectives of this research are synthesis the conceptual framework of virtual telehealth game and develop a framework for virtual telehealth game. The research method has two phases: 1) Synthesis of the conceptual framework of virtual telehealth game. This is in three components: virtual technology telehealth and game for health. 2) Develop the conceptual framework of virtual telehealth game. The researcher found that the conceptual framework for virtual telehealth game consists of 4 components: 1) Objectives of Virtual Telehealth Game. 2) Targeted behavior of Virtual Telehealth Game. 3) Targeted health of Virtual Telehealth Game and 4) Evaluation of Virtual Telehealth Game.

Author Keywords: Virtual Telehealth Game and Game for Health

articleTitle: Assessment of Learning Achievement of Inquiry-based Instruction on the Topic ‘Polymer’ in Science for Business and Services Online Course for Vocational Certificate Students
abstract: The purpose of this research was to study the learning achievement and satisfaction towards studying Science for Business and Services Course online on the topic ‘Polymer’ of vocational certificate students after being treated through the inquiry-based instruction. The research sample consisted of 15 first-year-vocational-certificate students of Food and Nutrition Major at Chitralada Vocational School by simple random sampling technique. The experiment took six hours. The research instruments were a learning management plan, an achievement test and a satisfaction questionnaire towards Science for Business and Services Online Course on the topic ‘Polymer’. Data were analyzed by a computer program. The research statistics used were percentage, mean and t-test. The research found that 1) students' learning achievement in Science for Business and Services Online Course on the topic ‘Polymer’ after using the inquiry-based instruction was higher than before, with the statistical significance at. 05. 2) the satisfaction of first-year-vocational-certificate students towards Science for Business and Services Online Course on the topic ‘Polymer’ was at the high level with the mean score 4.46.

articleTitle: The Development of Instructional Model for Engineering Materials Course by using Concept Mapping to Enhance Computational Skills
abstract: The research aimed 1) to develop a instructional model: Engineering Materials course by using a concept mapping to enhance computational skills, 2) To study the effect of using the instructional model: Engineering Materials course by using a concept mapping to enhance computational skills. Research tools used in this study were 1) learning management plan, 2) a computational skill knowledge test and 3) a questionnaires on satisfaction toward the instructional model. Data were analyzed using statistics percentages, mean, standard deviation and dependent t-test. The results of this research were as follows 1) the efficiency analysis results of the instructional model developed by the researcher have E1/E2 efficiency of 81.54/73.08. 2) The computational skills of the students after applying instructional model: Engineering Materials course by using a concept mapping was statistically significant at. 01 level and higher than pre-learning. 3) The students opinion toward instructional model: Engineering Materials course by using a concept mapping was the good level.

articleTitle: The Problem-Based Learning by Using Computer-Aided Engineering: The Heatsink Design Competition
abstract: In this paper, we proposed the problem-based learning(PBL) activity to train the critical thinking skill of first-year engineering students by using computer-aided engineering(CAE). The activity challenged the students to design the best heatsink on the topic “The Heatsink Design Competition.” The heart of the activity was divided into two important parts. The first part focused on researching and analyzing the necessary information such as the factor of thermal convection, the thermal conductivity of a material, etc. The second part was to synthesize the information by asking themselves some questions; for example, “how to choose the appropriate material?” “what are the key factors of the best heatsink?” etc. After that, CAE was applied to design a model and simulate the scenarios based on physics principles under their teachers' advice. Finally, this activity may help engineering students catch up with fast-changing technology.

articleTitle: Evaluating Learner Reasoning Skills through the Active Learning Flipped STEM Classroom Design
abstract: Developing learners to be the innovative thinkers through classroom activities is very challenging for educators. The active learning flipped classroom combined the STEM-learning activity design in this study then aims to investigate the learner reasoning skills. The results from the survey rated by samples of 396 learners studying at the undergraduate level at Prince of Songkla University, Thailand enrolled in the class of the Creative Problem Solving showed some significance in terms of the six domains of (1) Analysis reasoning, (2) Innovative thinking, (3) Decision making and judgment, (4) Mathematical reasoning, (5) Problem solving, and (6) Information researching. The reasoning skills of analysis and mathematics were related to the information researching. Interestingly, the improvement of decision-making and judgment skills were based on the learners' reasoning skills. In addition, the innovative idea of learners has been confirmed that was in accordant with not only the skills of decision making, but also the reasoning itself. Based on the experimental results, the designed approach in this study can also enhance learners to share their ideas with their classmates for giving comments and critiques on their assigned work in the classroom. Ultimately, the design thinking process can also encourage and stimulate learners to innovate new types of products or services through classroom activities more effectively.

articleTitle: A STEM CLIL Pilot Project in Ecuadorian High Schools
abstract: Following changes to education regulations in Ecuador, schools have had to increase their English language teaching provision, and CLIL has become a core requirement. As a result, there has been an increase in the number of schools teaching STEM subjects in English to predominantly Spanish-speaking students. Oxford University Press commissioned materials to help support and market their English language STEM textbooks to Ecuadorian schools. Two STEM events were developed, a science show for younger students and a biology workshop for older students. Both projects were piloted successfully. The science shows were launched at four high schools, and the biology workshop was offered as a teacher training event. All of the pilot events were well-received. Unfortunately, the project is currently paused due to schools moving to virtual teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, it is hoped that it can be reinstated when schools fully return to in-person classes.

articleTitle: Development of a prototype of Self Balancing Robot for Education
abstract: This research was aimed 1) to design and develop a prototype of Self Balancing Robot for Education, 2) to evaluate the effectiveness of prototype of Self Balancing Robot for Education and 3) to try out prototype of Self Balancing Robot for Education. The research and development process are divided into 4 steps: 1) Design the structure, 2) Analysis and design of the control system using the complementary filter, 3) Installation and assembly of equipment for develop PID control system and calculate parameters by Ziegler-Nichols method with trial and error tuning method and 4) Testing and improving the performance of the control system. This research applied materials and equipment that are available in the market. The Aluminum structure is 100 x 40 x 45 centimeters. From testing the performance of the Self Balancing robot. Found robot able to move in all 4 patterns. Turn left, turn right, walk backward and forward at a speed of 10 m/min. And used in teaching, found the overall satisfaction with a sample size of 26 students, found the teaching materials of the prototype of Self Balancing Robot was at a good level. (X = 3.88, S.d. = 0.49) Suitable for use as a teaching material in courses related to robotics and industrial control systems.

articleTitle: Information Engineering Course Management in Faculty of Engineering, KMITL towards excellence
abstract: This article represents the management of Information Engineering course in faculty of Engineering, KMITL towards excellence. Sample group is the parental units of who registered since 2017 until 2020 for 15 people, by purposive sampling. The researcher later presenting the Information Engineering course management. Then make a parental satisfaction assessment form about the Information Engineering course management in faculty of Engineering, King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang, towards excellence of 7 subject. The conclude of assessment says that the parental units are having a good level of satisfaction and the arithmetic mean is 4.72 and the standard deviation is 0.56 (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{X}$</tex> =4.27, S.D. = 0.56)

articleTitle: Problem Smartphone Use, Executive Function, and Academic Achievement of STEM Undergraduate Students
abstract: Smartphone use has become ubiquitous among college students, with several reports suggesting that students spend over six hours per day on their devices. However, the potential effects of extended engagement with of smartphones on cognitive ability and academic achievement are not well understood. In this research we compared problematic self-report smartphone use in two groups of undergraduate students (STEM and humanities). The groups had very similar demographics in terms of age and sex, and similar mean GPA scores. However, there was a strong negative association between problematic smartphone use and GPA in the STEM students, which was not seen in the humanities students. Furthermore, this association in the STEM students was found to be related to self-reported executive functions- impulse control and sustained attention. We speculate that problematic smartphone use may cause academic problems disproportionately for STEM students because it reduces cognitive resources, which are particularly important to achieve higher grades in fields such as science technology engineering, and medicine.

articleTitle: MiniScript: A New Language for Computer Programming Education
abstract: Computer programming is fundamental to modern STEM (science, technology, engineering, & math) education and industry. Visual programming environments such as Scratch provide a gentle introduction to the topic for young children, but the transition to text-based languages such as Python or C# can be a difficult leap. A new scripting language, MiniScript, has been designed to fill this gap. It uses minimal syntax and a carefully selected small set of language features to present a less intimidating challenge for the learner. At the same time, the language is complete enough to be used for sophisticated games and other programs. Finally, MiniScript itself is lightweight and designed to be embedded into other software written in either C# or C/C++, making it more likely that children will encounter the language in the context of games, thus providing self-motivated learning opportunities.

articleTitle: The Desirable Characteristics of Vocational Internship Students Contributing to the 21st Century Skills Development in Bangkok, Thailand
abstract: This research aimed to: (1) examine the construct validity of supervisors’ satisfaction according to the desirable characteristics of vocational internship students and the 21st century professional development in Bangkok, Thailand; (2) test the influence of supervisors’ satisfaction according to the desirable characteristics of vocational internship students on the 21stcentury skills development; (3) investigate the moderating effect of enterprise sizes on the linkages between supervisors' satisfaction according to the desirable characteristics of vocational internship students and the 21st century skills development. Survey research was conducted with 400 samples, who were supervisors working in enterprises categorized by size, located in the Bangkok Metropolis. The data collection via Google forms was employed, using the multi-stage sampling technique. The structural equation modelling (SEM) with maximum likelihood (ML) estimation via AMOS software was employed for the statistical analysis. The results revealed that (1) the structural validity testing of the desirable characteristics of vocational internship students construct and the 21stcentury skills construct were highly consistent with the literature. That is, both the desirable characteristic of vocational internship students and the 21stcentury skills had 4 dimensions and 16 items. (2) The influence testing found that the desirable characteristics of the vocational internship students had a statistically significant positive influence on the 21stcentury skills. (3) The results of the influence testing of enterprise sizes as the moderator roles indicated that the relationship between the desirable characteristics of the vocational internship students and the 21st century skills is moderated by enterprise sizes.

articleTitle: Practical Learning Model for Stimulate Innovative Idea of Technician to Reduce Loss in Manufacturing
abstract: This paper proposes a practical learning model for stimulate innovative idea of technician to reduce loss in manufacturing. The content is about the model of creating activities, learning process from work experience in problem-solving. The model incorporates Kolb's experience learning cycle theory into practice. Learning activities is arranged to promote the development of problem-solving skills and create an important incentive to realize the importance of correct and standardized solutions. The goal is to reduce the time to solve problems when occur problems and the waste of raw materials. As a result of this activity, technicians can analyze the cause of the problem, collaborate to find solutions and prevent problems directly by creating standard operating procedures. After applied standard operating procedures, there are fewer problems in the sealing process of canned beverage causing from adjusting the seamer machine, as well as reducing the waste of raw materials and the time for solving the problems following as the target.

articleTitle: Online virtual practicum during COVID-19: the case of a student work practice program Chitralada Technology Institute
abstract: Professional experience training is very important for vocational education students, who will train and practice according to job characteristics in field of studies to be skillful and gain job experience in technical level. However, due to the COVID-19 situation, having the professional experience training onsite as usual couldn't be done. So, the redesigned of training process has been made into the online version for students by using virtual practicum system, by assigning online electrical work which is as practical as the actual onsite one to students under their residential conditions, which will analyze the 8 electrical operations in total. The research has 37 participants, which are students at professional certificate level in Electrical Power, Chitralada Vocational School, Chitralada Technology Institute. The participants have been divided into 2 groups; first group, 22 students with professional experience training by using virtual practicum comparing with the second group, 15 students with professional experience training onsite. The process consists of 5 steps; Preparation, Accepting the assignments, Reporting the performances, Following up, and Evaluation. The professional experience training using virtual practicum in the academic year B.E. 2563 has the achievement averagely at 80.82%, which studied and compared the achievement with students who had professional experience training onsite in academic year B.E. 2562; averagely at 78.93%. From the result, it is found that at the statistical significance of 0.05, the average achievement of the virtual practicum isn't different comparing to the actual training, showing that the virtual practicum is as practical as the onsite training and can be used for students to gain experience and skills instead of the onsite training in the future.

articleTitle: UV-Visible Spectrophotometric Inquiry-Based Learning via STEM CAMP: Imitation of Syrup Drinks
abstract: STEM (Science Technology Engineering Mathematics) activity is one of the approaches to science learning. It promotes students' 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-century skills which lead to the development of innovation in the country. STEM activity together with inquiry-based learning (IBL) creates an effective learning experience. In the IBL-STEM activity, the laboratory instruments were used to enhance students' understanding in using a spectrophotometer and the concepts of the wavelength of light in nature, the concentration of the solution, and the quantification of the ppm (parts per million). It was found that IBL-STEM activity promoted critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration skills in students. Moreover, students had a better understanding of handling laboratory instruments, making the standard calibration curve, and interpreting data. This STEM activity broadened students' perspectives of the deployment of science and innovation. Also, it prepared students as life-long learners.

articleTitle: A Development of the Learning Management Model with Imagination Beyond Reality Technique for Development to Innovation for Beginners
abstract: This research aims to learners practice developing their thinking skills by using the model of learning management with imagination beyond reality technique for development to innovation for beginners. The sample group used in this research consisted of 54 students in the first and second year of high vocational certificate studying in information technology for career management in the academic year 2020. The research instruments consisted of 1) Innovative thinking exercise 2) Information retrieval exercise and 3) Presentation evaluation form. The analysis was designed using the 6W2H principle. The results of the research showed 1) The model of learning management developed, experts had a consistent opinion that the suitability within the acceptable criteria and 2) The learners had higher skills of thinking using imagination beyond reality than before and they were satisfied with the developed learning management at a high level. Therefore, it can be concluded that the developed learning management model it can be used to train students to develop thinking and can develop ideas into concrete both in terms of education and linking with the business sector according to the education 4.0.

articleTitle: “What is the best way to boil water?” A Home-based Activity and Collaborative Learning on Energy Efficiency
abstract: This study presented an inquiry-based activity on the topic of energy efficiency, which was one of the lessons in the Green Chemistry, an online mini-course for high school students. The experiment “What is the best way to boil water?” asked students to explore the energy efficiency of various heating devices they had at home such as electric kettles, electric stoves, rice cookers, and microwave ovens. Students also designed experiment to investigate variables that could influence the value of energy efficiency. This home-based activity led to a diverse experimental design with each group using different equipment and procedure. The online discussion provided an opportunity for collaborative learning. Students could gain further insight to the technical problem of saving energy in boiling water by comparing results from other groups. In addition, the discussion session also served as a forum for other relating issues such as energy waste from human behavior.

articleTitle: Application of Convex Mirrors to Study the Magnitude of the Milky Way Using STEM Education
abstract: This research aims to apply the use of convex mirrors in the study of the Milky Way's magnitude, which integrates knowledge using the STEM Education process to create a tool that helps to capture images of the entire Milky Way galaxy. These images can then be used to analyze the data. The analysis revealed that the Milky Way galaxy has a magnitude of about 4-5.

articleTitle: Development of Search and Inspection Set for Small Equipment and Tools in the HRS Pump Production Line: A Case Study of Lumentum International (Thailand) Co., Ltd
abstract: This article discusses the development of a search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools used in Lumentum International (Thailand) Co. Ltd. HRS Pump production line. The objectives were to 1) develop a search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools used in the HRS Pump production line; 2) assess the efficiency of the search and inspection kit; and 3) determine the user satisfaction level utilizing the developed search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools. The research tools include 1) iBeacon technology-based search and inspection kits for small devices; 2) an assessment form for experts; and 3) a satisfactory assessment form for users. The findings revealed that 1) the test result of a search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools in the HRS Pump production line, including an iBeacon transmitter, scanner receiver, data store, and web display, is within the acceptable range; 2) the qualitative testing result from experts revealed that the developed search and inspection kit is efficient; and 3) the users were most satisfied with the developed search and inspection kit. It can be concluded that this developed search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools used in the HRS Pump production line can be operated in actual industrial applications and the technology installed in the developed kit has no effect on other equipment and tools, and promotes faster and more efficient work.

Author Keywords: development of a search and inspection kit for small equipment and tools

articleTitle: Adoption of Teaching and Learning Using E-learning in Educational Systems: A Case Study of E-learning in The LEB2 of King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi
abstract: The Learning Environment B2 (LEB2) is an electronic learning (E-learning) platform for online teaching and learning. The objectives of this study are to examine the adoption of teaching and learning in LEB2 E-learning, and to study the factors affecting the adoption of teaching and learning in the LEB2 E-Learning. The research was conducted by applying the Technology Acceptances Model (TAM) theory with the sample group of King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi's faculty members and students A sample of 400 participants had access to the LEB2. The research methodology involved data collection with questionnaires, followed by descriptive statistical analysis and multiple regression. The results of the study revealed that three of the factors studied (Perceived Usefulness (POU), Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU), and Behavior Intention) influenced the adoption of LEB2 among respondents at King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi.

articleTitle: Digital Literacy in Austrian Lower Secondary Education - A Synthesis and Evaluation of Experiences in the First Two Years
abstract: It does not happen very often that there is a chance to analyze the introduction of a brand-new subject. When Austria implemented the mandatory curriculum “Digital Education” in September 2018 for all students in lower secondary education, digital literacy finally found its official way into additional grades. The curriculum covers digital competences, media competences, as well as civic education. Schools can decide if they offer stand-alone subjects or if they implement the curriculum in an integrative way in several other subjects. This paper reports on first experiences with the new curriculum by evaluating a survey conducted approximately two years after the implementation. Aiming to do so, the qualitative data were interpreted, summarized, and discussed, while the quantitative data were analyzed in former papers. The study was sent to 133 local public schools, whereas 117 teachers were willing to complete the questionnaire and 39 filled out the comment section. The following research questions lay out the basis for the evaluation of the qualitative data: 1) How do teachers manage the implementation of the new curriculum? 2) What is the teachers' opinion on the current situation? The results we present in this paper suggest that there are still people who fight with the new subject and that there are various problems that have to be tackled. Still, the attitude towards the current situation of the new curriculum is very positive.

articleTitle: The Development of Teaching Model using Research-Based Learning in the Illumination System Design
abstract: This research aims to develop students' learning ability to find information for problem solving by using research-based learning in illumination system design. The developed model is divided into 3 parts: Context, Learning Process and Learning Outcome. The researcher determined the activities according to the model, which could be divided into 4 activities: activity 1 was a research study, activity 2 was research proposal writing, activity 3 was conducting research, and activity 4 Presentation of Research Results. After developing a pattern and setting a learning activity, the researcher sent it to a specialist to examine its suitability. The experts agree that a Research-Based Learning model for illumination system design is suitable at the most level. After that, the researcher has calculated the scores from each activity according to the formula, the average score of E1/E2 is 83.75/87.68 above the threshold set at 80/80. The practice score was an average of 76.91, which was higher than the set threshold at 75 and the students had the most level of satisfaction with the model.

articleTitle: Applying Experiential Learning Cycle for Electrical Measurement Laboratory
abstract: This paper presents the content development of an electrical measurement laboratory using the concept of experiential learning. Each practice is designed as the learning cycle in which students will start by experiencing physical interaction, reflecting their idea from observations, and then surveying existing methods in order to implement an improved experiment. Two realization cases are explained based on different hardware/software settings. Finally, learning outcomes and issues are discussed as observed from the instruction of the past two semesters.

articleTitle: A Study of the Micro-Teaching Practice Ability of Teacher Training in Electrical Engineering Students by Teaching and Learning According to the Assessment for Learning Using Feedback Techniques
abstract: The purpose of this research was to study the ability to micro-teaching practice of teacher training in electrical engineering students by teaching and learning according to the assessment for learning using feedback techniques using the relative change score calculation. The target group of study was 12 students enrolled in Teaching Practice 1 in academic year 1/2020. The micro-teaching practice process requires students to practice at least 2 rounds of each skill. The assessment was done by a teacher who gave feedback in conjunction with the observer teacher. The feedback provided by Fisher, D., Frey. N. (2011) consists of 4 steps: 1) Feed up, 2) Checking for understanding, 3) Feedback, and 4) Feed forward. Students will practice in sequence started at motivation skills, information skills, questioning during teaching skill, creating activities skill, feedback skill, and lesson plan skill. Then students will take a teaching exam within 30 minutes. The research results were found that 1) the suitability of each skill observation tool was the highest level on average, 2) The students had a developmental level in micro-teaching, calculated from a relative change score, and had a development score of more than 60%. 3) Rater Agreement Index (RAI) for all skills is between 0.711 to 0.906, and 4) The satisfaction value of the students was achieved with a mean satisfaction of 4.72 S.D. 0.158 was a very satisfying level.

articleTitle: Current Status of Engineering Education in Jordan
abstract: Jordan’ Human Resources Development (HRD) Strategy 2016-2025 emphasizes the importance of developing a highly skilled workforce. Over the course of several decades, Jordan has developed slowly and produced numerous engineers annually. Preparing graduates of engineering for the multidisciplinary nature of modern societies' problems is challenging in engineering education. The article presents evidence that, despite the low demand on engineers in Jordan, the production of engineers at both undergraduate and graduate levels has increased quite dramatically over time. Recommendations are proposed for improved engineering education to develop engineers who can compete effectively with other careers in the competitive engineering market. Data have shown that Jordanian universities ought to promote quality and accredited education and training on a scale to meet the demands of its next generation of engineering skills and the current relationship between industry and academia needs to be reformed to achieve the required partnership in an effort to inspire reforms in engineering education.

articleTitle: Digital Game-Based Pedagogy: Teachers' Perspectives
abstract: Various business simulation games are contained in the curriculum to establish the pedagogy in the field of business process conception. The introduction of online business simulation games that simulate real business processes to inexperienced students has been established in digital pedagogy as well. The instructors were observers of the play by purposely selected students in the action research workshop while the researcher took the role of facilitator. After observing the workshop, the instructors were interviewed. They saw the teamwork and the phenomenon that students were helpful and cooperating well. While playing the game, they discussed all about the business issues, decisions, status of the business and segregation of duty. Additionally, in order to be ready for digital pedagogy using digital games, the teacher needs to work on demonstration, assistance and consultation for a while to be familiar with the game. Meanwhile, the concerns of digital games are license fee and accessibility to the game and communication.

articleTitle: Research on Highly Efficient Deep Learning Engineering Teaching for Information Management and Information System Undergraduates
abstract: The education of deep learning engineering is an important direction for Information Management and Information Systems (IMIS) undergraduate education in universities in recent years. This paper investigates the specific methods to realize the education of deep learning engineers based on the existing teaching plan for Information Management and Information Systems undergraduate students through teaching cases. The methods and means of constructing deep learning knowledge system and engineering practice experience at each stage of undergraduate education are specifically analyzed. The results of the study show that deep learning engineers can be effectively trained by introducing targeted teaching contents and engineering practice cases into the existing undergraduate teaching plan of Information Management and Information Systems. The study is expected to provide a reference for the education of deep learning engineers in related teaching plan.

articleTitle: A Novel Chirp Demodulation Scheme Based on SAGC for Amateur Radio Data Transmission
abstract: Based on the sinusoidal automatic gain control scheme (SAGC), an equalizer implementation and a chirp demodulator have been proposed. With the 1-unit constant of SAGe output amplitude, an application as an equalizer has been implemented in order to eradicate the unwanted cut- off frequency characteristic of an amateur radio. According to loss of radio reception caused by the multipath fading phenomenon, a chirp modulation has played an important role to attenuate strong interferences in wireless communication. Thus, chirp demodulation based on modified SAGC has also been proposed in this paper. The equalizer application's result shows that the chirp signal amplitude has been stabilized to 1 unit at any carrier frequencies. Furthermore, the sawtooth wave has been recovered by using SAGC chirp demodulation before comparator and sample & hold block generate the information data. By the SNR range from 1 dB to 10 dB, the BER of the proposed SAGC chirp demodulation scheme is lower than the conventional one.

articleTitle: Self-training in Sports Agility Drills using Smartphone Sensors
abstract: Traditional agility tests often use the stopwatch to measure the time consumption for each training scheme. The stopwatch can be manually controlled by staff coaches, which has more uncertainty. The automatic measurement system can be replaced to reduce human error. However, it is more expensive and should be used under control by technical staff. Moreover, in this pandemic situation, social distancing needs to be applied to prevent the COVID-19 from spreading. In this paper, we propose the method to apply the smartphone sensors for sports training, which can be applied for remote practices and self-training. We demonstrated the popular agility training as a 10-m agility shuttle run drill and described the assumptions of the corresponding ideal acceleration characteristics. After that, the actual training data was illustrated and analyzed for evaluating the trainee's agility. More than twenty volunteers were employed to study the feasibility of self-training. The results show that more than 90% of volunteers can effortlessly use our method. Although the data analysis by themselves is quite difficult for nonexperienced users, the training data can be analyzed by the professional instructor via the online platform.

articleTitle: Affordable microfluidic electroanalysis for senior high school, college and university STEM education
abstract: Microfluidics is the theory and practice of fluid management in microscale flow channel assemblies for advanced applications in clinical, pharmaceutical and environmental analysis and nano- and biotechnology. Electroanalysis, on the other hand, is a potent alternative to optical detection and on integration into cheap and portable analytical devices, has been developed into routines for personal health care and intensive care monitoring, field testing of pollutants and assays for industrial biofermentation and chemical synthesis control. Work with microfludics and electroanalysis, separately or in a functional fusion, needs knowledge in the core subjects of STEM education. For young and eager students at schools and universities laboratory experiments involving an affordable merger of the two techniques is a perfect chance for exposure to many modern topics in science and engineering R&D and to grasp the importance of a highly multi- and interdisciplinary approach to problem solving. For the representative case of electrochemical microfluidic heavy metal trace analysis we describe here the construction and operation of a low-cost microfluidic detection system that can be considered as a component of an exciting STEM training, especially in developing countries with tight educational budgets.

articleTitle: The Efficiency of Music Learning in a Blended Learning Environment of Undergraduate Students In Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat University
abstract: This research aimed 1) to investigate the efficiency of music learning in a blended learning environment; 2) to assess how technology can facilitate knowledge sharing between the teacher and the students in blended learning environment; and 3) to study the students' attitudes towards the music learning in a blended learning environment. The sample was 14 second - year students who enrolled in course 2071103: introduction to western music theory in the first semester of the 2020 academic year, in western music program, faculty of humanities and social sciences, Phranakhon Si Ayutthaya Rajabhat university, selected by using a purposive sampling technique. The research instruments were 1) lesson plans, 2) pretest and posttest, 3) teacher performance evaluation form, and 4) a questionnaire on students' attitudes towards a blended learning environment. The statistics were mean, percentage, Standard Deviation (S.D.), and t-test with one sample test. The research results were 1) The students' posttest score were higher than the pretest. The findings were statistically significant difference at. 05 level; and 2) The students' opinions towards towards a blended learning environment were at a very high level (X = 4.50, S.D. = 0.62), including 1)The teaching technique (X = 4.67, S.D = 0.61), 2) The assessment (X =4.54, S.D = 0.48), and 3) The generic skills (X = 4.47, S.D = 0.65) respectively.

articleTitle: The Feasible Study to Use The IP Camera for Doing The Online Physics Experiment
abstract: This pandemic time, the face to face learning has many constraints. Several online applications possibly do the lecture course. It can give the benefit as well as in-class learning. However, it is impossible to provide hands-on experiments, which is a significant objective of the laboratory. This paper proposes the feasibility study to apply the IP camera for doing online physics experiments of first-year engineering students. The simple harmonic motion experiment was an example for this study in order to recover the laboratory objective. The IP camera's pan and tilt functions are employed to do the experiment as a student's hand. Free mobile and computer applications, such as EYE4, are used as the student's eyes to observe the experiment's object movement. These are similar to hands-on interaction. This study found that this method is low cost and easy to modify and maintain the experiment by physics teachers. In addition, using the IP camera with physics experiments turns general online learning into hands-on interaction physics experiments to continuously train students' practical skills. The most beneficial of using an IP camera with a physics experiment is that the students can do the physics experiment from their homes in this global pandemic. However, this method depended on the internet speed, the smartphone performance, and the quality of the IP camera.

articleTitle: Teaching basic mechanics with Lego
abstract: Incorporating didactic tools such as Lego pieces allows to motivate the learning of basic physics concepts. This work shows an integrated proposal to teach mechanics concepts using experiments carried out with Lego pieces. The proposal is approached in four stages. First, students build mechanisms using Lego pieces. Subsequently, the movement of the mechanism is analyzed by video analysis using the Tracker software. In the third stage, the theoretical model associated with the mechanism is built, analyzed, and solved using computational tools such as Mathematica or MATLAB, at the end the theoretical results are compared with the experimental results. In the final stage, the physical concepts are evaluated through an evaluation system built on the Canvas platform. Some of the studied experiments are launching of objects by a catapult, lifting of objects by means of a pulley system, movement in the crank-rod mechanism, movement on an inclined plane, analysis of movement with obstacles, movement on a roller coaster. At the end of this work, the results in learning and in the development of disciplinary competencies of the students who participated in the educational experience are discussed.

articleTitle: Gamification Ecosystem for Research-based Learning
abstract: This research aims to synthesis and design a gamification ecosystem for research-based learning. The methods for conducting research are as follows: step 1 synthesis of gamification ecosystem for research-based learning. And step 2 design the gamification ecosystem for research-based learning from step 1. The results 1) the synthesis of gamification elements consisted of 10 elements: goal, learning, achievement, challenge, progress indicator, competition, engagement, time management, personalization, and micro-interaction and 2) research-based learning activities consisted of: initial RBL competencies of learner, redesign of the basic learning modules, assignment of the practical project, project execution and feedback and evaluation

articleTitle: Using Augmented Reality Technology in Learning Archeological Places
abstract: The purpose of this research is to use augmented reality (AR) technology in learning archeological places of 9 places including Wat Thewarat Kunchorn, Wat Sukhantharam, Wat Benchamabophit Dusitwanaram, Wat Mai Thong Sen, Wat Ratchaphatikaram, Morphon House Palace, Suan Sunandha Palace, Parusakawan Palace, and Wat Bot Samsen. Each place can see the history of the content through VDO and 3-D models that can be viewed 360 degrees. They presented it through the learn archeological places guidebook. The sample groups of the research were 30 students of bachelor's degree in industrial education program, Rajamangala University of Technology Phra Nakhon. The research results showed that the learn archeological places guidebook was at a high level (the mean equaled to 4.36) and the students' satisfaction with the learn archeological places guidebook was at a high level (the mean equaled to 4.13).

articleTitle: Instructional Package for Self-Practicing and Online Learning of Electric Motor Control Course: A Case Study of Chitralada Technology Institute on Covid-19 Situation
abstract: The purpose of this study is to present how to implement practical learning with the use of ‘Instructional Package for Self-Practicing and Online Learning of Electric Motor Control Course on COVID-19 Situation: A Case Study of Chitralada Technology Institute’. This study hopes to help relieve the problem of students who are prevented to attend practical classes on campus, due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This study was conducted with an Electric Motor Control course, the instructional package includes a practical electrical motor control panel, instructor's manual, learner's manual, exercise worksheets, and a pre-test and post-test. The instructional package was then implemented as apart of the learning process of the sample group. The sample group was specifically selected consisting of 20 vocational students studying in their second year at Chitralada Technology Institute. The following are the findings of the study: 1) The results of the study on the Instructional Package has an efficiency rate of the highest, (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{x}=4.82$</tex>, S.D = 0.33) higher than the stated hypothesis, 2) the developed instructional package was efficient with 78.12; 3) post-test scores were significantly higher than pre-test scores by 0.05 and 4) the students rated their satisfaction with using the instructional package as the highest. (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{x}=4.54$</tex>, S.D = 0.64)

articleTitle: STEM Communication Skills and The Rhetorical Triangle: Key-Elements to Meet Business's Expectation
abstract: This article is a mixed-method study (quantitative and qualitative) focused to explore the correlation, associations, and effects of Rhetorical Triangle as key elements in the 21st Century science communication skills of the STEM undergraduate students (n=282) in a university in Bangkok and in Business's expectation / communication skills needed (n=27). The results verified positive and significant level of Students' communication skills and the needs in Business's expectation to the key elements (Ethos, Logos, and Pathos) towards the requirements in Sale force, Promotion, Public Relations, and Internal Communications in various Business Types. Implications of the study enabling and predict what are for the students to prepare and be a work-ready in communication skills after graduated.
